speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The SOP Act introduced a fast and low-cost adjudication mechanism to deal with payment disputes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For a typical construction project, the developer pays the main contractor, who, in turn, pays its subcontractors or suppliers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As a construction project can take several years to complete, progress payments are made periodically throughout the project duration.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Parties along the value chain often fund their own work first and collect payment thereafter.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, it is critical that parties are paid in a timely manner for work done or goods supplied.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: When the Act was first introduced, the industry was unfamiliar with how the adjudication process could assist them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Over the years, industry players are now more aware that adjudication is an effective mechanism to resolve payment disputes quickly, compared to arbitration or litigation which can be lengthy and expensive.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In the initial years of administering the Act, there were less than 100 applications per year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This has now increased to more than 400 applications per year since 2014.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We are happy to see that the industry is increasingly using the Act to resolve their payment issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, from time to time, there have been calls by stakeholder groups to amend the SOP Act to enhance the effectiveness of the Act in facilitating cash flow.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, we initiated a review of the SOP Act and have consulted stakeholders extensively over the last five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In all, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) conducted four rounds of industry consultations and six focus group discussions with stakeholders, including developers, architects, engineers, main contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, adjudicators and the Singapore Mediation Centre which administers the adjudication process.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, different stakeholders may have different views and perspectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) Law Reform Committee published a list of proposed amendments to the SOP Act in September 2015.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Committee raised concerns that the current approach of allowing a limitation period of six years for claimants to submit a claim for work done was too long.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In this regard, it suggested reducing the limitation period from six years to one year so that respondents would not have to manage claims for an unreasonably long period after works have been completed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: But the feedback from the industry was that one year would be too short as settlement of final payments for the projects tended to take much longer.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is a reasonable period, taking into account the time to settle final payment claims and the defects liability period, which typically ranges from 12 to 18 months.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This illustrates the approach that we have taken in coming up with the amendments that are before the House today.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We have considered and incorporated feedback from stakeholders into our amendments where possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In doing so, we have tried to strike a balance between the interests of the varied stakeholders while ensuring that the amendments enhance the effectiveness of the adjudication mechanism as a low-cost and speedy dispute resolution mechanism for the construction industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Broadly speaking, the amendments focus on three areas: first, expanding and clarifying the scope of the application of the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, we are proposing amendments that will expand the scope for more contracts to be applicable under the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Singapore has been making a big push to raise productivity and quality in the built environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Construction Industry Transformation Map (ITM) launched in October last year set out the strategies to help our construction industry move up the value chain and capture growth opportunities in Singapore and abroad.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The scope of the SOP Act will be amended to support the Construction ITM.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Internationalisation is also a key thrust of our construction ITM.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Given our small domestic market, firms will need to venture overseas in order to grow in size.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, clause 3 will also cover prefabrication works that are carried out locally for projects overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The coverage for local prefabrication works for export will only be applicable when both contract parties are locally registered entities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will facilitate the enforcement of the adjudication determination in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Another amendment, also at clause 3, will make clear that claims for work done or goods supplied before contract termination are valid.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is to address any ambiguity on the point as to whether claimants can apply for adjudication upon contract termination.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: That said, we understand that it is common industry practice for contract terms to suspend payment until a later date if a contractor has defaulted, leading to the termination of the contract.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: When this happens, the SOP Act will pay heed to terms pre-agreed by parties.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This means that claimants that have defaulted on the contract will need to abide by contract terms, and they will be able to submit a payment claim under the SOP Act only after the conditions in the contract have been met.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Another issue that this Bill will address is the lengthening of the adjudication process due to submission of complex claims.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We have observed that some claimants have started to include complicated prolongation costs, damages, losses or expenses when applying for adjudication.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This goes beyond the original scope of the SOP Act, which is intended to cover claims for work done or goods and services supplied.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In contrast, a typical adjudication case takes only about 21 to 28 days from application to payment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, clauses 11 and 14 will make clear that adjudicators are to consider claims on damages, losses and expenses only when the claim is supported by documents showing the parties' agreement on the quantum of the claim, or a certificate or document that is required to be issued under the contract.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Parties that wish to dispute on complex claims should consider other avenues, such as arbitration or litigation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The second set of amendments will deal with the handling of payment claims and responses.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, the Act requires claimants to serve payment claims according to the contract terms.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Typically, a contract will stipulate a specific date or fixed period for payment claims to be served so that employers can better manage payment claims from multiple subcontractors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, there have been past cases where claimants unintentionally serve their claims on the wrong date.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This technically invalidates the payment claim during adjudication.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Such issues have also been raised before the Courts, leading to payment delays.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In such cases, the payment claim will be deemed as served on the contract specified date or on the last day of the fixed period.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To illustrate, if a contract specifies that the payment claim must be made on the 29th of the month, the payment claim will still be valid if the claimant serves it before the 29th of the month.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, the respondent's deadline for payment response will only start running from the 29th of the month.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: If the claimant serves a payment claim on the 30th of the month instead of 29th, his claim will be treated as being served in the next month.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We have also heard feedback from the industry stakeholders on the need for the Act to clarify the status of repeat payment claims.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will preserve claimants' entitlement to seek payment through adjudication so long as the payment claim is served within the limitation period, is unpaid, and has not been adjudicated upon its merits.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The third set of amendments deals with changes to the adjudication process.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, the SOP Act only allows for respondents to apply for adjudication review if they disagree with the adjudication determination and wish to have it reconsidered.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The SAL committee had proposed that claimants should also be eligible for adjudication review.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, clauses 12, 15 and 16 will allow claimants to also apply for adjudication review.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: With the amendment, it is possible to have a scenario where both the respondent and the claimant are entitled to adjudication review.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: If both parties submit a review application arising from the same determination, only one adjudication review will be conducted.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Regardless of the party that initiated the review, the appointed review adjudicators will consider submissions from both parties in arriving at an assessment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We are also updating the SOP Act to align it with Court decisions that were based on provisions in the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, there have been cases where claimants have made administrative errors in their adjudication applications, such as failing to provide an extract of the contract which was relevant to the payment claim when applying for adjudication.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, the Court noted that the failure to submit such an extract did not prejudice the respondent and should not invalidate the application.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, clause 10 will empower adjudicators to accept an adjudication application that lacks certain information or documents prescribed in regulations, if the adjudicator is satisfied that the respondent is not materially prejudiced.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: I will share another example where we have taken in the judgments from the Courts in our amendments.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The SOP Act is meant to facilitate timely payment to claimants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: At the same time, the Act gives respondents the opportunity to raise objections to justify non-payment to claimants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, the Act only states that the respondents cannot raise objections for withholding payment in the adjudication stage if these objections were not flagged earlier in the payment response stage.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, we are concerned that payment to claimants would be delayed in the event that respondents raise objections late in the adjudication process.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is in line with comments made by the Courts in recent decisions and will also advance the intent of the Act to facilitate speedy dispute resolution.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Respondents that are affected by this amendment can still seek recourse through other channels like arbitration or litigation after paying the adjudicated amount.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We will also be making changes to improve the operation of the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, the interest rate for late payment is often based on the interest rate stipulated in the contract.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We have received feedback that interest rates set out in contracts can be as low as 1%, as subcontractors may have less bargaining power in setting the rates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: A higher interest rate will be used if it is stipulated in the parties' contract terms.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This amendment will encourage respondents to pay claimants on time.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This amendment will also bring our SOP regime in line with practices in other jurisdictions, such as New South Wales and Queensland.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will allow parties to be more mindful about the dos and don'ts when preparing payment claims, adjudication applications and the relevant responses.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These grounds are consistent with those that have been developed by the Courts over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The intention is to stipulate a non-exhaustive list, so the Act will not bar the development of case law.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This remains the principle that underpins the amendments we are introducing today.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I would, first, like to commend BCA on the public consultation that it conducted in June 2018 on the proposed amendments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Following the consultation, BCA provided responses to key feedback received and refined some proposed amendments after hearing the public's suggestions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am heartened by BCA's engagement with the public in crafting this Bill and believe that the process has resulted in a stronger piece of legislation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have just three clarifications on the proposed amendments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: During the public consultation, it was suggested that the adjudication review start afresh when the majority of the panel of review adjudicators is replaced.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: BCA responded that if the replacement adjudicators need more time to bring themselves up to speed, the review adjudicators can seek an extension of time subject to the consent of both the claimant and the respondent.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If parties can consent to extending time to allow review adjudicators to be brought up to speed, why not also allow parties to consent to having the review start afresh?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: BCA had stated that this keeps adjudication speedy and low cost by removing the need for adjudicators to consider complex loss and expenses claims.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Small Claims Tribunal (SCT) has jurisdiction to hear a tort for damage caused to property, which includes claims for losses or expenses incurred by owners of property as a result of careless, reckless or improper acts by others.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is no requirement that the claims for losses or expenses be supported by written agreement on the amount.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is also able to hear claims arising from oral agreements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The SCT is similarly intended to provide an efficient and inexpensive channel to resolve consumer-supplier disputes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The power of SCT to consider loss or expenses claims in the absence of clear documentation does not seem to impede the expediency of the tribunal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, can the Ministry of Finance (MOF) clarify why loss and expenses claims should be beyond the power of adjudicators to assess?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If these claims cannot be resolved by the adjudication process, parties have to resort to arbitration or litigation, as MOF has stated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As pointed out by BCA, these matters are slightly more complicated, which will incur even greater costs for parties if they have to adjudicate or litigate these claims.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are precisely the cases that require a simpler and cheaper dispute resolution process.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would be more efficient for all heads of claims relating to the same dispute to be heard by a single body.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While the second limb implies that there should be no fault on the part of the respondent in failing to raise the objections earlier because they could not have known of these reasons, the first limb is not clear on the element of the respondent's fault.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can MOF clarify whether section 19(6A)(a) requires that the new circumstances arose out of no fault of the respondent?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The amendments had taken the uneven balance of negotiating power between main contractors and subcontractors into account.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I appeal to the Ministry and relevant Government agencies to consider extending advisory assistance to our subcontractors and guide them with familiarising themselves on their rights and deserved payments.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They should and can work with the Government agencies to minimise their losses and avoid worsening their cash flow crunch and falling into financial difficulty.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The construction industry suffers from many problems and disputes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This Bill seeks a fairer allocation of risks to subcontractors and easier settlement of payment disputes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is because in reality, there are many complex underlying issues which have been unresolved.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Besides unrealistic contract periods and tight manpower resources which have very serious safety implications, both during the process of construction and in the distant future, the parties involved pass the buck in pushing responsibilities for defects and payments.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One common example is the deliberate delay in payment by the owner and main contractor.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To make the situation worse, the funds received by the main contractor for specific work done are diverted for other uses instead of paying the subcontractors.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some projects were tendered at a loss due to miscalculations.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Others were tendered at unrealistic fees because the main contractors just wanted incoming funds to stay afloat for as long as possible.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether it is possible to allow parties to consent to starting the review afresh when a majority of the review adjudicators have been replaced or, in other words, when two out of three adjudicators on the panel have been replaced.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Presently, the Act does not set out the processes following the replacement of adjudicators.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The intent is to ensure that the adjudication proceedings are not unduly delayed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Should a longer period be needed to make a determination, the review adjudicators may seek an extension of time, subject to the consent of both the claimant and respondent, as Mr Louis Ng has rightly pointed out.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The review adjudicators are best placed to decide on the period of extension required, depending on the needs of the case.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is, in fact, more flexible than starting the review afresh, as the extension could be shorter than 14 days, which is the default period should a review be started afresh.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This would avoid unduly delaying payment to the claimant.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is less than 1% of all adjudication cases.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Louis Ng also noted that SCT has jurisdiction to hear claims on damage, loss and expense that are not supported by written document and asked why adjudicators must disregard such claims under the SOP Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As mentioned in my earlier speech, this restriction is to reduce delays in the adjudication process.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, we have seen delays of up to 129 days due to the inclusion of such claims.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Allowing such claims to be heard under the SOP Act clearly goes against the intent of the SOP Act to provide speedy dispute resolution and facilitate cash flow.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There are also several key differences between claims under the SCT Act and the SOP Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The quantum and corresponding complexity of the claims under both Acts are quite different.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For instance, the claim limit for disputes brought to the SCT is $10,000, or $20,000 if all parties consent.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: When the SCT (Amendment) Act 2018 comes into operation, the claim limit will be $20,000, or $30,000 if all parties consent.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But there is no limit on the claim amount under the SOP Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is not uncommon for damage, loss and expense in a construction contract to exceed millions of dollars.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Adjudicators under the SOP Act are also required to meet statutory timelines and complete their determinations within set timelines.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In this regard, it is reasonable for such complex claims to be dealt with outside the ambit of the SOP Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Louis Ng asked to clarify if the objections raised by respondents to a payment claim based on new circumstances must arise out of no fault of the respondents.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The purpose of the amendment is to encourage respondents to raise any objections to payment claims at the earliest opportunity to facilitate the fast resolution of payment disputes between the parties.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Thus, belated objections from respondents must not be within the respondent’s knowledge or control.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, if an adjudicator considers a claim for damage, loss or expense that is not supported by any document showing agreement of the parties, the adjudicator has failed to comply with the provisions of the Act in making the adjudication determination.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In such an event, it would be considered a new circumstance beyond the respondent’s control, and he could raise this as a valid objection in a review adjudication or an application to Court for setting aside.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh has rightly pointed out that parties further upstream in the construction value chain typically have more bargaining power in negotiating contracts with their subcontractors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In this regard, the subcontractors may prefer more amicable settlement of disputes before resorting to adjudication, arbitration or litigation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While the SOP Act cannot change such dynamics entirely, it has been useful in facilitating cash flow in the industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: By upholding the rights of parties in the industry to seek payment for work done or goods supplied, the Act has helped deter parties from delaying or withholding payment without valid reasons.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But in order for this to be effective, claimants need to exercise their rights and apply for adjudication when required.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh has also suggested for the Government to extend advisory assistance and to raise awareness amongst subcontractors on their rights to payment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On this note, BCA will be enhancing the current guide on the SOP Act on its website to make it easier for contractors to understand.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA will also work closely with industry associations to provide firms with information on how adjudication can be used as an effective means to settle payment disputes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In addition, BCA will also conduct briefings to familiarise the industry with the amendments that are before the House today.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh has also suggested to put in place measures to prevent funds meant for a construction project from being diverted for other uses.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have examined this issue as part of the review.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I beg to move.
